texts.preamble: Bheemsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 April, 2018 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Bench At Indore Cr.R No.732/2018 Indore, dated : 04/04/2018:-
texts.facts: Unsuccessful applicant for getting relief from two Courts below has approached this Court by filing the present revision petition. Facts of the case in brief are that on 09.09.2004 at about 7:20 in the morning, Food Inspector stopped the applicant who was going to sale milk and took a sample which was later found adulterated. This order of the Appellate Court is under challenge in the present petition.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he does not want to press the merits of the case. He submits that the applicant belongs to a very poor family and is a small milk vendor. He goes door to door to sale milk. He is the only bread winner of the family and has two school going children and old aged parents fully dependent on him. He does not has any other source of income. His family does not HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE possess any agricultural land. His whole family is dependent on milk selling. His business has got stuck and his family is facing serious financial crises due to his detention. He is punished for the offence under sections 7(i) read with 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The incident took place in the year 2004 and since then he is continuously facing the trial. He has no criminal history and no other criminal Bheemsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 April, 2018 He is also ready to pay the enhanced fine amount. Learned public prosecutor has not challenged the facts submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant.
